_comentario: MODELO TEENS. Aula IMPAR = modelo de FALA (REGRA 29): dialogo line-by-line + 3 role-plays, sem texto central. Vozes iguais as aulas 1-4: 'ellen' remapeada para voz de adolescente (12 anos), 'candy' para a segunda voz jovem (Ruby), 'arthur' intocado para as palavras soltas do Word Arena e para o adulto do listening 2. DOIS grids de vocab (4+4): o revealVocab do shell teens so conhece vocabGrid1 e vocabGrid2.

lesson.menu_desc: A friend who has never been here asks what your street is like -- there is and there are with quantifiers -- 27 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- New City, New Street
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Sophia | Lesson 5 -- New City, New Street
lesson.grammar_point: there is / there are with quantifiers

listenings.text: When we moved, it was only four miles, but it felt like another country. On my old street there was a bakery on the corner, and there were a lot of children my own age, so I was never inside the house. On the new one there is nothing on the corner, and for the first month I thought there was nobody under forty on the whole road. But the park is within walking distance, the library is two blocks away, and there isn't much traffic, so my mother lets me go on my own. It took me about three months to stop hating it. And the funny thing is, the street did not change at all. I did.

Welcome to the neighborhood walk. The whole route is six blocks and it takes about forty minutes at an easy pace. Start at the square behind you. On this first street there are a lot of small shops and two cafes, and the building on the left with the green door is the oldest one here. Now, on the second street, please be careful. There is only one crosswalk, at the far end, so cross there and never in the middle of the block. After that the park is within walking distance, about three minutes. One last thing. Do not do this walk at rush hour, between six and eight, because the sidewalks are crowded and there is too much traffic noise to hear anything I say.

items.situation: Somebody asks what there is on your street. Give two things and one quantity.
tips: There's a doorman in my building and there are two crosswalks on my block.
There are a lot of small shops, but there aren't many trees.

items.situation: It is eight in the morning and nothing is moving. Say why, in one sentence.
tips: There's a lot of traffic because it's rush hour.
It's rush hour, so the avenue is completely blocked.

items.situation: A friend asks if your street is quiet at night. Answer with a negative.
tips: There isn't much noise after ten.
There aren't many cars at night, so it's quiet.

items.situation: You want to talk about the shop on the corner but the word will not come. Describe it.
tips: There's a place on the corner where you buy bread.
It's the shop that opens at six in the morning.

items.situation: Somebody asks if there is a park near you. Say yes, and say how near.
tips: Yes, there's one within walking distance.
There are a few, and the closest one is two blocks away.
